CausalChain: Circadian nutrient signals -> Increased hepatic PPARβ/δ activation -> Upregulation of lipogenic enzymes -> Elevated synthesis of PC (18:0/18:1) -> Release of PC (18:0/18:1) into circulation -> Activation of muscle PPARα -> Enhanced fatty acid uptake and β-oxidation in muscle -> Improved systemic lipid metabolism
Hypothesis: Timed activation of hepatic PPARβ/δ enhances the circadian production of bioactive PC (18:0/18:1), which in turn activates muscle PPARα to boost fatty acid oxidation, thereby providing a novel therapeutic approach to correct dyslipidemia and mitigate metabolic syndrome.
Abstract: Metabolic homeostasis relies on intricate communication between the liver and peripheral tissues, mediated by nuclear receptor signaling and lipid metabolites. Recent evidence suggests that hepatic PPARβ/δ regulates the circadian expression of lipogenic enzymes, leading to the synthesis of bioactive lipids such as phosphatidylcholine (PC 18:0/18:1). This lipid mediator appears to facilitate muscle fatty acid uptake and oxidation through activation of muscle PPARα. Here, we propose that enhancing the circadian amplitude of hepatic PPARβ/δ activity to boost PC (18:0/18:1) production may synchronize insulin-sensitive muscle fatty acid oxidation. Timed nutritional or pharmacological interventions aimed at modulating this hepatic-myo inter-organ axis could provide a novel strategy for ameliorating dyslipidemia and metabolic syndrome.
